blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: `Shipment` has one constructor, `Shipment(String senderPostcode, String recipientPostcode, int weightGrams)`. A new caller writes `new Shipment(order.recipientPostcode(), order.senderPostcode(), 1_200)`. The team's tests create shipments from postcode literals of their own and check each field. What happens to this caller's code?

options.text: It compiles, and the tests pass, since no check compares what each String means with the field it lands in
options.says: both arguments are String, so the call matches exactly; a test with its own literals reads back what it passed in either order

options.text: It compiles, and the tests fail, since a swapped call puts each postcode into the other one's field
options.says: the tests never call this caller's code; they build shipments from their own literals, which round-trip either way

options.text: It is rejected by javac, since the getter names passed in disagree with the parameter names
options.says: javac matches argument types to parameter types; names play no part

options.text: It is rejected by javac, since two adjacent String parameters make the call ambiguous
options.says: the call matches the one constructor exactly, like the page's five-argument call with adjacent Strings, which compiles

origin.section: Same-Typed Constructor Arguments Swap Without an Error; a Builder Names Each One

questions.stem: `RetryPolicy.Builder.maxDelay(Duration d)` throws if an initial delay has been set and `d` is shorter than it; `initialDelay(...)` and `build()` check nothing. A config loader calls the setters in the order the keys appear in the file, then `build()`. One file has `max-delay: 1s` on the line above `initial-delay: 5s`. What does loading it produce?

options.text: A policy with its initial delay above its maximum, since maxDelay() ran before an initial delay was set
options.says: the setter compares against the part set so far, and nothing was set yet; build() checks nothing, so the policy is created

options.text: A policy with delays that pass the check, since initialDelay() then compares the two delays as well
options.says: initialDelay() checks nothing, and maxDelay() ran first, so the check passed against no initial delay

options.text: An exception from maxDelay(), since that setter compares the two delays and finds them in the wrong order
options.says: when maxDelay() ran, no initial delay was set, so there was nothing to compare against

options.text: An exception from build(), since build() is the one call that sees both delays and compares them
options.says: build() here only calls the constructor and checks nothing

origin.section: A Builder Checks the Whole Object in build(), Where Every Part Is Set

questions.stem: `Playlist`'s private constructor does `this.tracks = Collections.unmodifiableList(builder.tracks)`. A DJ app keeps one builder, builds tonight's playlist from it, then adds two encore tracks to the same builder for tomorrow. What does tonight's playlist list now?

options.text: Tonight's tracks only, since unmodifiableList took a read-only copy of the tracks at build()
options.says: unmodifiableList returns a view of the same list, not a copy

options.text: Tonight's tracks only, since the builder starts a new list once build() has used its list
options.says: the builder keeps adding to the list the playlist wraps

options.text: Tonight's tracks and the encores, since the playlist reads the list the builder writes to
options.says: the view forbids writes through the playlist, but the builder's writes to the list underneath show through

options.text: Nothing new: adding the encores throws, since the builder's list became unmodifiable at build()
options.says: only the view refuses writes; the builder keeps writing to the list underneath it

origin.section: A Builder Used Again After build() Changes What It Built, Unless the Product Copies

questions.stem: A metrics exporter keeps one `HttpRequest.Builder` with the URI and a token, and for each push calls `builder.header("X-Batch", batchId).POST(body).build()`. After the third push, which `X-Batch` values does the third request carry, and which does the first request, still held by a retry queue?

options.text: All three batch ids on the third; the first still has only its own, since build() took the builder's state at that moment
options.says: header() adds a value to the builder each time, and each build() copies the builder's state into an immutable request

options.text: All three batch ids on the third; the first now has all three too, since every request reads the builder's headers
options.says: build() copies the state; the first request does not change when the builder does

options.text: Only the third batch's id on the third; the first still has only its own, since header() replaces the earlier value
options.says: header() adds; setHeader() is the method that replaces

options.text: Only the third batch's id on the third; the first now has that id too, since every request reads the builder's headers
options.says: header() adds rather than replaces, and a built request does not follow the builder

origin.section: HttpRequest.Builder Copies on build(), but a Reused Builder Keeps Adding Headers

concepts: HttpRequest.Builder.header() adds a value, so a reused builder sends every earlier value too, while each built request keeps the state it had at build().
Two adjacent constructor parameters of the same type can be swapped at a call site without a compile error or a failing round-trip test, and the object is built with the wrong values.
A check in a setter compares against whatever has been set so far, so a cross-part rule placed there passes when the setters are called in the other order, and a missing part gets through as null.
Collections.unmodifiableList is a read-only view of the same list, so the builder's later writes show through it.
